name: Mishael
overview: The name Mishael appears in Scripture referring to several individuals who demonstrate faithfulness and service to God in different contexts. He is first mentioned as a son of Uzziel who assisted Moses in carrying the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp, showing reverence for God's holiness (Exodus 6:22; Leviticus 10:4). Later, a Mishael stood alongside Ezra as the law was publicly read to the people, indicating a commitment to God's covenant (Nehemiah 8:4). Additionally, Mishael, also called Meshach, was one of the three Hebrew youths trained with Daniel in Babylon, who remained faithful amid trials, helped interpret Nebuchadnezzar’s dreams, and endured the fiery furnace rather than compromise their allegiance to God (Daniel 1:6-7, 11). These passages highlight Mishael’s role as a faithful servant in both Old Testament worship and exile contexts.
